every_owner_is_checked_on_disk: the module refuses to publish if any named owner is missing, because a register pointing at modules nobody wrote would be exactly the fake completion S027 §38 is guarding against

failure_mode.FAIL_looks_like: run work, Claude notices a problem, Claude writes a fifty-point steer, work resumes, repeat
failure_mode.PASS_looks_like: work, evidence, HCLI diagnoses, HCLI generates probes, HCLI prepares the next model, HCLI runs them, the user optionally observes
failure_mode.the_count_is_not_the_metric: handing off fourteen mechanical operations while keeping every judgement is not progress toward autonomy; it is a faster scaffold. The metric that matters is whether HCLI can run a cycle without a decision escalating, and this register does not claim it can.
failure_mode.where_this_campaign_sits: between them, and closer to FAIL than the handed-off count suggests. Fourteen recurring operations now have owners, but the five that remain are the ones that decide what happens next: designing a candidate, noticing a new instrument defect, setting a claim boundary, adjudicating two disagreeing harnesses, and ruling an obligation met. Those are the loop, and Claude is still in it.

how_this_falls_honestly: an operation moves out of the Claude column only when a module OWNS it - not when a module mentions it. The five remaining entries have no owner and are listed rather than dropped, so the count can only fall by real handoff.
